chunks: Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Faddal narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Walid, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
"When the child reaches five cubits (in height), his slaughtered meat is eaten (i.e., is valid), and when he reaches ten years, his will is valid."
ai.seo_question: At what age is a child's will considered legally valid in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* delineates the thresholds of partial legal capacity (*ahliyyah*) for minors, distinguishing between physical maturity markers and cognitive understanding. While the consumption of slaughtered meat at five cubits reflects a practical standard of physical growth, the validity of a will at ten years signifies the onset of discernment (*tamyiz*) regarding property disposition, a key concept in Shia fiqh for determining when a child can manage limited assets.
